guard: The runtime half of `two agents MUST NOT share a worktree concurrently` is real: the spawn-time guard refuses a live holder's tree as L4008, the refusal reads presence liveness so a dead holder releases with no bookkeeping, the holder registry is fed at spawn and reseeded at adoption, and the handle carries the logical worktree into the journal
proveWith: pnpm mutation-proof --config implementations/runtime/smoke/mutations/mesh-worktree.json   # --config resolves against the repo root, never the cwd
why: Lane F durable-actions step 8 (2026-09-03): the SPEC 6.5 worktree binding is a logical
contract with one rule, and the runtime enforces the half the validator cannot see. Each
obligation has a mutant: the guard call itself (W1), the presence-liveness read that makes a
dead holder's tree reusable rather than locked forever (W2), the registration that makes the
guard able to refuse at all (W3), the adoption reseed that keeps a resumed run enforcing what
its journal shows (W4), and the handle spread that carries the worktree into the journal and
the turn client's L4004 (W5). All five mutate mesh-handler.ts, which the suite imports through
a relative `../src` path — no build sits between the mutation and the run.

mutations.name: the spawn guard is never consulted
mutations.expectRed: the second spawn refuses as the effect's own L4008, naming the tree and its holder
mutations.cell: the second spawn refuses as the effect's own L4008, naming the tree and its holder
mutations.note: The one call site that enforces the rule at spawn. Measured 2026-09-03: both refusal cells red — the live-holder L4008 and the adopted-registry L4008 — 7 passed, 2 failed.

mutations.name: the liveness read is inverted, so a dead holder still blocks its tree
mutations.replace: if (true || rows.some((p) => p.card?.name === holder.name && p.lifecycleUid === holder.uid))
mutations.expectRed: a spawn into the dead holder's tree performs: sequential reuse is legal
mutations.cell: a spawn into the dead holder's tree performs: sequential reuse is legal
mutations.note: Presence IS the release: nothing else ever unbinds a tree. Measured 2026-09-03: both sequential-reuse cells red — the dead holder's tree and the lapsed adopted holder's tree stay refused — 7 passed, 2 failed.

mutations.name: a fresh spawn never records its holder
mutations.find:
if (typeof handle.worktree === "string")
      this.worktreeHolders.set(handle.worktree, { name: parseAgentHandle(handle.agent).name, uid: parseAgentHandle(handle.agent).uid });
mutations.expectRed: the second spawn refuses as the effect's own L4008, naming the tree and its holder
mutations.cell: the second spawn refuses as the effect's own L4008, naming the tree and its holder
mutations.note: With no registration the guard has nothing to refuse over. Measured 2026-09-03: exactly one cell red — the live-holder L4008 — and the adoption block stays green because its holder arrives through the journal reseed, 8 passed, 1 failed. The single red is why W4 exists separately.

mutations.name: adoption never reseeds the holders, so a resumed run stops enforcing its journal
mutations.expectRed: the adopted holder registry refuses a spawn into the recorded live holder's tree
mutations.cell: the adopted holder registry refuses a spawn into the recorded live holder's tree
mutations.note: The other feed line, deletable separately from W3. Measured 2026-09-03: the adopted-registry L4008 cell reds, and the block's follow-up cell reds with it because the unrefused intruder then holds the tree against the successor, 7 passed, 2 failed.

mutations.name: the handle loses its worktree, so the journal and the turn client ride bare handles
mutations.expectRed: the settled handle carries the logical worktree into the journal
mutations.cell: the settled handle carries the logical worktree into the journal
mutations.note: The spread is what everything downstream reads: registration, the journal record, and the turn client's cross-tree L4004. Measured 2026-09-03: six cells red across four blocks — the journal cell, both spawn-holds cells, the live-holder L4008, the cross-tree L4004 (the yield succeeds instead), and the lapsed-holder reuse cell whose handle comes back bare — 3 passed, 6 failed.
